title: feat: point the agent at Ninja Forms' own abilities (#3003)
body:
Closes #3003

## Summary
Teaches the agent about Ninja Forms. Ninja Forms registers its own 32 `ninjaforms/*` abilities (create and edit forms, fields, actions, calculations, submissions, import/export, embed, settings), so this PR adds **no new form-creation ability**. It only makes the agent aware of them.

- `includes/Models/skills/contact-forms.md`: rewritten. Ninja Forms is the recommended plugin; the skill tells the agent to find `ninjaforms/*` with `ability-search` and run them with `ability-call`, lists the abilities by task, and records the rules the ability descriptions impose (merge-tag spacing, action field names, the two-step `remove-field` workflow and its confirmation phrase, export results being content not files, never printing secret settings, keeping children's data out of notification emails). `sd-ai-agent/create-contact-form` stays documented for WPForms, Contact Form 7 and the HTML fallback.
- `includes/Core/AbilityPluginRegistry.php`: Ninja Forms catalog entry (`ability_count` 32, `has_abilities` true); WPForms wording changed to "supported when already active".
- `includes/Automations/EventTriggerRegistry.php` + test: a "Ninja Form Submitted" automation trigger on `ninja_forms_after_submission`, registered only when Ninja Forms is active. This is the one addition that is not an ability; drop it if you would rather keep this PR to the skill and catalog entry.

`includes/Abilities/ContentAbilities.php`, its tests, `phpstan.neon` and the PHPStan stub from the first revision of this PR are reverted (no diff against `main`).

No identifiers were renamed.

## Tested through the agent (not just Ninja Forms directly)
Ran against real Ninja Forms 3.16.1 on WordPress 7.0 in wp-env (admin user), calling the agent's own entry points: `ToolDiscovery::handle_ability_search` / `handle_ability_call`, and `AbilityFunctionResolver::execute_ability()` with `FunctionCall` objects for the `wpab__sd-ai-agent__ability-search` / `ability-call` tool names. **65 of 65 checks passed** once the three opt-in abilities below were enabled.

- **Discovery:** all 32 abilities are visible to an admin and classified by the agent's permission model (27 auto-run, 5 destructive). Ten natural-language queries ("create a contact form", "form submissions", "embed form on page", ...) each surfaced NF abilities, and `select:` returns full input/output schemas.
- **Every ability executed through `ability-call`:** `create-form` (text, email, dropdown, textarea fields), `list-field-types`, `list-forms`, `get-form`, `add-field`, `update-field`, `reorder-fields`, `update-form`, `list-actions`, `add-action`, `update-action`, `add-calculation`, `update-calculation`, `list-calculations`, `duplicate-form`, `get-submissions`, `get-submission`, `get-submission-fields`, `update-submission`, `export-submissions` (CSV and JSON), `process-submission`, `export-form-definition`, `import-form`, `embed-form` (both steps, shortcode written to the page), `get-public-link`, `get-plugin-settings`, `update-plugin-settings`.
- **Confirmation gate:** `delete-action`, `delete-calculation`, `delete-form`, `delete-submission` and `remove-field` are refused with `ability_requires_confirmation` and succeed only after one-turn approval. `remove-field` returns Ninja Forms' export-first workflow and completes with the exact phrase from `next_step`.
- **Function-call envelope:** `ability-search` and `ability-call` work through the resolver, including an empty-args object, the `parameters` alias, a self-correcting `ability_invalid_input` error carrying the schema, and the destructive refusal.
- **Roles:** a subscriber and an editor neither see nor can run `ninjaforms/list-forms`.

Findings:
1. `ninjaforms/delete-form`, `update-submission` and `delete-submission` are marked `mcp.public = false` by Ninja Forms by default. The agent honours that: they are hidden from `ability-search` and `select:` (22 of the first 25 returned). A site enables one with the `ninjaforms_mcp_public_*` filters; I verified with a temporary mu-plugin that they then appear and pass the same checks. The skill now says so, so the agent does not work around it with `run-php`.
2. The harness is a one-off and is not committed: Ninja Forms is not installed in this repo's PHPUnit environment, so these checks cannot run in CI without new test infrastructure. Not done: a live model-driven chat (no provider credentials in the isolated environment); the checks exercise the same dispatchers the loop calls.
3. Ninja Forms itself logs PHP warnings (undefined keys in its email action) when `process-submission` is given a partial email setting; that is Ninja Forms code, not the agent path.

## Worker self-verification
- PHPUnit: Tests: 4819, Assertions: 23025, Errors: 0, Failures: 0, Skipped: 119, Incomplete: 1 (existing)
- Lint:    PHP clean (`composer phpcs`). JS and CSS lint, build and bundle budgets were last run on the first revision of this PR (all passed); this revision changes no JS, CSS or `build/` file (only PHP, one skill markdown file and a test).
- PHPStan: 0 errors
- Agent-path harness: 65 / 65 checks (see above)

## Notes
- WPForms support is untouched: other sites using this plugin may already run it.
- Consumer: the CEF chapter template now uses Ninja Forms only (superdav42/tgc.church#1416).

title: GH#3006: feat: add-credit popup when SD AI credit runs out
body:
## Summary

When SD AI credit runs out mid-chat, a popup now opens. One click takes the user to checkout, the plugin picks up the new balance when they come back to the tab, and one more click continues the request that failed.

Resolves #3006

## Before: what we found testing it

We walked through the journey with a scripted browser on the local site, simulating a job that fails with `credit_exhausted`:

1. The chat showed only an inline notice: "Good news—as an early adopter, use coupon code EARLY … leave a review." No popup appeared.
2. Its main button, "Redeem EARLY coupon", opened a new tab at `#/settings`, which shows the **General** tab.
3. The user then had to find and click the **SD AI** tab.
4. There, **Redeem Coupon** was the primary button and **Add credits** was a secondary button in 4th position.
5. Add credits → service email confirmation (tracked separately on the service side).
6. After paying, nothing noticed the new balance or resumed the chat.

## After

1. Credit runs out and the popup opens: **"You've used your SD AI credit"**, showing the current balance and the buttons **Not now** / **Add credit**, plus a **Have a coupon code?** link with an inline field.
2. **Add credit** gets the one-time `purchase_credits` URL and opens checkout in a new tab. The tab is opened during the click so popup blockers don't stop it, and `opener` is cleared.
3. The popup switches to "Finish checkout in the new tab". When the chat tab gets focus back, it re-checks `/superdav-account`; there is also a manual **I've added credit** button. A notice explains if no new credit has arrived yet.
4. **Credit added** shows the new balance and **Continue my request**, which runs `retryLastMessage()` and resends the original request.

Other details:
- The inline notice now reads "You've used your SD AI credit. Add credit to keep working. Your conversation is saved." and its **Add credit** button reopens the popup.
- Users without `manage_options` see a single "ask a site administrator" message.
- On the account tab, **Add credits** is now the primary button and Redeem Coupon is secondary.
- Credit links now go straight to the SD AI account tab (`&tab=superdav-account`), via new localized `accountPageUrl` and `canManageBilling` values.
- The EARLY / $200 / review wording is removed from the chat notice, the embed widget, and the server and client failure messages.
- The popup code loads lazily as a separate ~7 KiB chunk. The launch bundle only gets the store state and a small host component. Bundle budgets were raised slightly, with the measurements recorded in `scripts/check-bundle-size.js`.
- `DESIGN.md` now documents how the popup behaves.

## UX verification (Playwright, local site, simulated credit exhaustion)

```
1 popup title: You've used your SD AI credit
2 checkout tab: sdaiagent.com/sd-ai/account/action/  (new tab, one click)
2 popup title after click: Finish checkout in the new tab
3 early check: "No new credit yet. Payments can take a moment to arrive…"
4 success (focus return, simulated +credit): "Credit added. You're all set. Available balance: $25.00." [Close] [Continue my request]
5 run POSTs before/after continue: 1 → 2
6 inline notice "Add credit" reopens popup: 1
7 floating widget: popup opens on credit exhaustion
8 account buttons: Open account portal [tertiary], Manage payment methods [secondary], Redeem Coupon [secondary], Add credits [primary]
page errors: none
```

## Out of scope / follow-up

After clicking Add credit, a first-time payer on an unlinked site still has to confirm their email by magic link and pick a package before reaching checkout. Those pages come from the managed service, not this plugin, so they are tracked separately.

## Worker self-verification
- PHPUnit: Tests: 4818, Assertions: 23025, Errors: 0, Failures: 0, Skipped: 119, Incomplete: 1
- Lint:    PHP/JS/CSS all clean
- PHPStan: 0 errors
- Build:   succeeded
- Bundle:  budgets passed

body:
## What

Readme-only update to the WordPress.org listing (competitor plan item A4). People searching for "WordPress AI agent" or "MCP" plugins don't currently find SD AI Agent, and the listing doesn't mention its main advantages.

- **Tags:** `ai, chatbot, assistant, automation, connector` → `ai, ai agent, mcp, automation, gutenberg`. "chatbot" attracts front-end chat buyers; competitors list `mcp` and `ai agent`.
- **Short description** (129 characters): "AI agent in wp-admin: build Gutenberg pages, manage plugins and WooCommerce. You approve changes, cap spend and undo any change."
- **Description bullets** added for undo, spend caps and the built-in MCP server.
- **Cost FAQ:** states the $10 of free SD AI credit added on activation (confirmed by David on 2026-11-18), the $10 top-ups and the spend caps.

Display name stays "SD AI Agent"; no slug, text domain or identifier changes.

## Claims checked against code

- Undo: `includes/REST/ChangesController.php` routes, `includes/Services/ChangeRevertService.php`, "Changes" menu item in `includes/Admin/UnifiedAdminMenu.php`.
- Spend caps: `includes/Core/BudgetManager.php` (daily and monthly) and the "Daily Budget Cap (USD)" field in `src/settings-page/settings-app.js` under AI Agent > Settings.
- MCP server: `includes/REST/McpController.php` (`POST /wp-json/sd-ai-agent/v1/mcp`, nonce or Application Password), registered in `includes/Plugin.php`. The copy deliberately doesn't claim claude.ai/ChatGPT web support (no inbound OAuth).

title: GH#3020: add next_steps recovery guidance to failed ability responses
body:
## Summary

Failed ability calls now return a bounded next_steps list. New AbilityErrorGuidance maps error-code naming conventions (not_found, not_configured, forbidden, invalid, missing, failed, ...) to recovery steps; abilities can override with next_steps in WP_Error data. Wired into AbilityFunctionResolver WP_Error, exception, tier-2 dispatch and static error paths. Validation failures that already carry a hint are unchanged.



## Files Changed

includes/Core/AbilityErrorGuidance.php, includes/Core/AbilityFunctionResolver.php, tests/SdAiAgent/Core/AbilityErrorGuidanceTest.php, tests/SdAiAgent/Core/AbilityFunctionResolverTest.php

## Decisions

Defaults come from code-name patterns instead of editing ~370 WP_Error sites; explicit next_steps override is the per-ability path. Only the next_steps key is read from error data so secrets in other keys are never forwarded. Skipped when a validation hint is present to avoid two competing instructions.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified: AbilityFunctionResolver::execute_ability() driven through a booted WordPress with the real registered sd-ai-agent/file-outline ability (missing file) returned code sd_ai_agent_file_not_found with next_steps and no hint; ability_not_allowed returned its explicit next_steps (AbilityFunctionResolverTest, 28 tests/103 assertions across resolver+guidance suites, 0 failures). title: fix: clearer one-click Advanced install, no GitHub release path
body:
## Summary

One-click install of SD AI Agent Advanced never worked: sdaiagent.com rejected every
site with "This site has not finished verification". Root cause and fix are in the
SD AI service (separate change): the service required a registration `verified`
flag, but the plugin registers sites as `self_declared`, so almost every
production installation was rejected.

This PR improves the plugin side of the flow.

### UX

- Button label is now **Install and Activate the SD AI Agent Advanced plugin**
  (**Activate the SD AI Agent Advanced plugin** when installed but inactive).
- Larger primary button (min-height 44px, 10px/24px padding) and more spacing
  around the status line and help text in the Advanced card
  (`src/settings-page/style.css`).
- Help text says Advanced is free with an SD AI account and that the install is
  confirmed on sdaiagent.com.

### No more GitHub release install path

We still publish the Advanced ZIP as a GitHub release asset, but the product path
is connecting the site to sdaiagent.com. Removed the manual GitHub/Upload Plugin
instructions from:

- the Advanced card (`src/settings-page/superdav-account-manager.js`)
- model guidance (`includes/Core/SystemInstructionBuilder.php`)
- `sd_ai_agent_advanced_plugin_required` errors (`includes/Abilities/WordPressAbilities.php`, `includes/Abilities/FileAbilities.php`)
- the chat suggestion chip fallback (`src/components/chat-redesign/message-items.js`):
  non-installers now get the chip sent to the model, which tells them to ask an
  administrator, instead of opening the GitHub releases page

### Defence in depth for the signed push

The service no longer relies on the registration `verified` flag, so the site now
also requires that an administrator here started the flow: minting an
`install_advanced` account action records a 30-minute install request
(`AdvancedPluginManager::record_install_request()`), and
`AdvancedInstallController` rejects pushes without one

active. `AGENTS.md` and `readme.txt` document the extra check.

title: fix: send replayed Responses function_call arguments as JSON objects
body:
## Problem

On 2026-11-20 a production conversation on `superdav-chat-standard` failed on every retry. The client showed "The AI provider is temporarily unavailable".

- The managed service's Sub2API pool hit the OpenAI account's 5h usage limit. It failed over to an Anthropic fallback account in the middle of the conversation.
- `SuperdavAiResponsesToolSearchTextGenerationModel::function_call_to_input_item()` encoded replayed arguments with `wp_json_encode( $call->getArgs() ?? new \stdClass() )`. A no-argument call decodes to `array()`, not `null`, so it was sent as `"[]"`.
- OpenAI accepts that in history. Anthropic rejects it with `tool_use.input: Input should be an object`, so the conversation stayed broken until the OpenAI limit reset.

The WordPress core OpenAI-compatible model already turns empty arguments into `{}` (`AbstractOpenAiCompatibleTextGenerationModel`). Only the custom Superdav Responses model had this gap.

The managed service now also normalises arguments at its edge (already deployed). This PR fixes the source so clients don't depend on that safety net.

## Change

- `includes/Infrastructure/AiClient/Superdav/SuperdavAiResponsesToolSearchTextGenerationModel.php`: the new `function_call_arguments_json()` always emits a JSON object.
  - `null`, `array()` and `""` become `{}`.
  - Associative arrays and objects are encoded unchanged.
  - JSON object strings pass through byte-for-byte.
  - Lists become numeric-key objects.
  - Invalid JSON becomes `{"raw": …}` and scalars become `{"value": …}`.
- `includes/Core/CompletedTurnCompactor.php`: `compact_argument_text()` now compacts only JSON object text, as its docblock already stated, and casts the result to an object. A numeric-keyed object can no longer be re-encoded as a list.

## Worker self-verification

title: feat: rebuild managed turns portably when the native provider is at capacity
body:
## Why

Users can switch providers at any time. For the managed SD AI provider, users only pick fast / standard / strong, and the service's fallback chooses the upstream provider.

Until now the managed service failed over to another provider by translating a request that was built for OpenAI Responses (deferred `tool_search` / `namespace` tools, encrypted reasoning, native item IDs). That translation is lossy, and translated output can leak into this plugin's native replay state.

This change uses the pattern OpenCode uses for provider switching. The client keeps provider-neutral history and rebuilds the request for the target, instead of passing one provider's native request to another provider.

## Change

- `SuperdavAiProvider`: adds `CLIENT_CAPABILITIES_HEADER` (`X-Superdav-Client-Capabilities: provider-switch`) and `PROVIDER_CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE_CODE`.
- `SuperdavAiResponsesToolSearchTextGenerationModel`:
  - Native Responses requests (create, poll and cancel) advertise the capability. The service then keeps native state on its own provider family.
  - When the service answers `provider_capacity_unavailable`, whether as a buffered 503 or as a failed background job, the turn is rebuilt from SDK history through the existing Chat Completions fallback (`generate_chat_completions_fallback()`). The native continuation cursor is cleared, so native replay never mixes with another provider's output.
- No UI changes: the switch is silent, and the model picker and billing tier are unchanged.

Older services ignore the header, so behaviour there is unchanged.

## Worker self-verification
- PHPUnit: Tests: 4827, Assertions: 23069, Errors: 0, Failures: 0, Skipped: 119, Incomplete: 1
- Lint:    PHPCS clean on changed files; no JS/CSS changes
- PHPStan: 0 errors
- Build:   not applicable (PHP-only change; no `build/` output changes)
- Bundle:  not applicable (no JS/CSS changes)

New tests in `ResponsesContinuationTest`:
- `test_provider_capacity_rebuilds_the_turn_portably_and_drops_native_state` checks the header on native requests, the Chat Completions rebuild from full history, that the capability header is absent on the portable request, and that the cursor is cleared.
- `test_background_provider_capacity_failure_rebuilds_portably`.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

`prepare_message_input_items()` folds thought-channel text into visible assistant content when replaying history. That is pre-existing and not a request error, but reasoning should not be replayed as visible text, especially across providers.

title: GH#3036 GH#3037: stop page-quality loop on render timeouts; health probe works on tenant runtimes
body:
## Summary

Resolves #3036
Resolves #3037
For #3038 (not fixed here; see the comment on the issue)

- `PageCompletionGate`: after `MAX_RENDER_INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURES` (2) consecutive quality reports whose only blocking findings are `frontend_render_failed`, `requires_repair()` returns false so `AgentLoop` stops re-injecting the repair prompt. The terminal notice says in plain words that the page was written but not published, the live site is unchanged, and to start a new chat and try again. Any other failure or a passing report resets the counter. `get_status()` exposes `render_unverifiable`.
- `theme-completion-iframe.js`: the load timeout is 30 s (was 15 s), and when it expires a parsed same-origin document (`readyState !== 'loading'`, body present) is accepted instead of failing. The `load` event waits for every subresource, which a phone on a slow network can delay long after the page is usable.
- Health probe: `PostMutationHealthCheck` sends a random 5-minute token (`X-SdAi-Health-Token`, transient `sd_ai_agent_health_token`); `HealthEndpoint` accepts a request from a non-loopback address only when the token matches (`hash_equals`). Tenant runtimes without a loopback listener now get `healthy` through the public URL. When the probe still cannot run, `describe()` adds a `note` that this is not evidence the site is down and the user must not be told to contact their host.
- Rebuilt `build/` artifacts.

## Why

A learner on a hosted tenant runtime asked the agent to publish a page. The preview iframe timed out at all three viewports, and the gate re-sent the same repair prompt 13 times while `site-loopback-check` answered `unreachable` (no listener on 127.0.0.1; the public `_health` URL returned 403). The model told the beginner to ask their host. Evidence is in #3036 and #3037.
